title: Apollo's Chief Economist Says AI Has Not Paid Off Outside Big Tech - How to Be the Exception
content:
One of Wall Street's best-known economists just said there is NO SIGN OF AN AI PAYOFF outside tech.
His name is Torsten Slok, chief economist at Apollo.
In his note on October twenty fourth, he compared the Magnificent Seven tech giants with the other four hundred ninety three companies in the S&P 500.
For the tech giants, revenue per worker is rising.
For the other four hundred ninety three, it is flat.
Profit margins show the same split. And he sees no sign yet of AI lifting productivity growth.
Here is the number that stood out to me.
According to Ramp data in the same note, the top ten percent of firms account for NINETY NINE POINT FIVE PERCENT of spending on model serving and inference.
So AI spending is heavily concentrated.
So is AI overhyped? Not exactly.
His point is that the AI story will be decided by ordinary companies, not the tech giants.
And he argues that business runs on judgment, context and trust, which a model alone does not supply.
Here are three practical implications for your team.
One. Stop measuring AI by how many people have a license. Measure one business number, like revenue per employee or hours saved per week.
Two. Do not buy the most expensive model by default. Many tasks work fine with cheaper or open models.
Three. KEEP HUMANS on judgment calls. Let AI do the drafting, searching and sorting.
Imagine an insurance claims team.
AI reads every document and drafts a summary. The adjuster still makes the decision, but each claim moves faster.
That shows up in the numbers.
Here's my take. The gap Slok describes is not a technology gap. It is an IMPLEMENTATION GAP. And that is exactly where the opportunity is.
